relevance_note: The paper describes one patient with Tangier disease and an ABCA1 variant: "a diagnosis of TD confirmed by a homozygous variant of IVS35+1G>A in the ABCA1 gene".
method_note: Hand extraction; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Two in-scope people: the trial participant ('patient', the single first-hand patient of this n-of-1 study) and a previously published Italian patient described in the Introduction with sex and features (labelled 'ref [5] patient'; the paragraph ends with [5], while [4] cites the miglustat product information). No variant row for 'ref [5] patient': the paper says only that 'genetic testing later confirmed TD' and prints no ABCA1 variant or gene attribution for her. The other UK adult patient ('only two adult cases known in the UK') and the participant's father ('My dad') get no rows: no individual-level facts / not tested or affected. Time-limited findings not recorded as excluded because they changed later: participant had 'no neurological symptoms until his teens, with normal nerve conduction at age 14' before developing neuropathy; the Italian patient's tonsils became 'normal in size and colour' on miglustat. Age at last evaluation left not reported: only age at baseline (21) is given, and follow-up continued about 3.75 years beyond it. Country of origin not recorded: 'A patient in the UK' gives residence, not origin. Variant type, pathogenicity left not reported: the only class statement ('loss-of-function variant') is a general statement about TD in the Introduction; IVS35+1G>A is printed in IVS notation, so cdna_hgvs_as_stated is null. Pancytopenia (Italian patient) not mapped to the thrombocytopenia checklist item. Study type recorded as 'other' (n-of-1 ABAB trial on a single patient). Prior publication = conference abstracts of the same study (WORLDSymposium 2024 abstract in Mol Genet Metab cited). No contradictions found.
